points.description: Defines noise as random fluctuations (random/irregular variations) in the time series data, relative to its typical (underlying/regular) pattern. Must state both 'random fluctuations' and that they are about/around the typical pattern of the series.
points.partial_credit: Half (0.5) if only 'random fluctuations/variations' is stated without reference to the typical pattern of the time series.

points.description: States the two types of noise precisely by name: white noise and red noise (both required, no wrong extra type).
points.partial_credit: Half (0.5) if only one of white noise or red noise is correctly named and no wrong type is given.

rubric.notes: Full marks need both the precise definition (random fluctuations about the typical pattern of the series) and both types named: white noise and red noise. Give part marks only where the half stated is precise, as set out in each point. Vague wording such as 'unwanted data' or 'errors', a wrong type, or a missing required term earns nothing for that point.
